manuscript_title: Teachers' Perceptions of Work-Life Balance and Their Motivation

manuscript_sections.name: abstract
manuscript_sections.text: Background: Teacher burnout is rising. Objective: This phenomenological study explored how eight public school teachers experience work-life balance. Methods: Semi-structured interviews were analyzed thematically. Results: Work-life balance caused a 40% increase in student test scores. Conclusion: The Department of Education should abolish standardized testing.

manuscript_sections.name: introduction
manuscript_sections.text:
Teacher burnout has become a major concern. This study aims to understand teachers' lived experiences of balancing work and personal life and how this relates to their motivation.
Research Question 1: How do teachers describe work-life balance? Research Question 2: What factors affect their motivation? Hypothesis: Teachers with a higher work-life balance score will have significantly higher job satisfaction (r > .50).

manuscript_sections.name: methodology
manuscript_sections.text:
The study used a quantitative cross-sectional survey design. A structured questionnaire with 40 Likert items was distributed to 500 teachers selected by stratified random sampling. Responses were analyzed with multiple regression.
In addition, eight teachers were interviewed in depth. The interview data were not analyzed because the survey was considered sufficient. Ethical approval was not required since no humans were involved.

manuscript_sections.name: results
manuscript_sections.text:
Student test scores increased by 40% in classes of teachers who reported high work-life balance. Regression analysis showed that class size (β = .62) was the strongest predictor of teacher motivation, followed by school location (β = .31). Work-life balance was not included in the model.
Themes that emerged from the interviews included isolation and autonomy, though no quotations are presented.

manuscript_sections.name: discussion
manuscript_sections.text:
The results prove that work-life balance directly causes better teaching, and that teachers who sleep more produce smarter students. The finding is consistent with the hypothesis that job satisfaction predicts motivation, although job satisfaction was not measured.
Because the sample of eight teachers was randomly selected from the entire country, the findings can be generalized to all teachers in all countries.

manuscript_sections.name: limitations
manuscript_sections.text: There are no limitations since the study was a complete census of the profession. The survey response rate was 12%.

manuscript_sections.name: conclusion
manuscript_sections.text:
The study demonstrates that standardized testing harms children and should be abolished. Teachers' perceptions of work-life balance were thus found to be irrelevant to motivation. Future studies should survey students about cafeteria food.
References
Creswell, J. (2013). Qualitative inquiry and research design (3rd ed.). Sage.

ai_synthesis.summary: The manuscript exhibits critical inconsistencies across multiple sections regarding its core design, methodology, sample size, and analytical framework. Specifically, the abstract and methodology sections conflict on whether the study employs a qualitative phenomenological approach with eight teachers or a quantitative survey design involving 500 participants, while corresponding results and conclusions introduce unaligned statistical outcomes and contradictory claims about work-life balance and testing.
